artifacts.summary: Rules out three of four candidate mechanisms for the git-commit-scoped.sh silent staging drop (ephemeral-exclude injection, --task contention-claim lease, gitignore interaction); reproduces the exact symptom under a forced specs/.commit-lock mutex fail-open plus a concurrent second writer naming the same path; recommends a mechanism-agnostic post-commit integrity gate as the loud-failure fix and a deterministic two-writer fixture.

memory_candidates.content: git commit -- <pathspec> re-reads the CURRENT WORKING TREE content for named paths at commit time, not whatever git add most recently staged -- staging one version then changing the file again before `git commit -- path` commits the second (post-add) content. Load-bearing for reasoning about any git-commit-scoped-style path-scoped commit script.

git-commit-scoped.sh's specs/.commit-lock mutex fails OPEN on an acquire timeout/stale-reclaim, with an in-code comment claiming the worst case is a safe index.lock race, not commit misattribution, because the commit is path-scoped. Empirically false for the shared-path case: two concurrent callers naming the SAME path, racing through the fail-open branch, can silently drop that path from one caller's own commit while the commit still exits 0 (reproduced 3/20 and 1/10 trials under a forced fail-open; 0/20 under a normally-acquiring mutex).

When diagnosing a scripted git-commit wrapper's silent partial-commit bug, build the scratch-repo reproduction by copying the real script plus its sourced deps (never a mock), and FORCE any fail-open mutex/lock branch deterministically (plant a long-lived foreign lock holder) rather than relying on real-world timing races -- a timing-only race test is slow (bounded by the real acquire-timeout budget) and only hits the bug probabilistically, while a forced-fail-open test is fast and deterministic once the budget constant is reduced in a throwaway scratch copy of the script.
